title: ‘Sentimental Value’ Star Anders Danielsen Lie and Anne Marie Ottersen Inducted Into the Haugesund Walk of Fame: ‘It Feels Full Circle’
description:
Norwegian actors Anders Danielsen Lie and Anne Marie Ottersen were inducted into the Haugesund Walk of Fame.. 

	The unveiling taking  place during
body:
Norwegian actors Anders Danielsen Lie and Anne Marie Ottersen were inducted into the Haugesund Walk of Fame.. 

	The unveiling taking  place during the first weekend of this year’s Norwegian Intl. Film Festival Haugesund,  Danielsen Lie and Ottersen were recognized for contributing to “building the professionalism and high standards of Norway’s acting community, both on the theatre stage and in the film and television industry,” noted the committee. They join the ranks of Liv Ullmann, Pål Sverre Hagen and Renate Reinsve.
	

	“Do I look back? I haven’t had much time to reflect on this yet because my life is so hectic at the moment. But I do remember releasing [his 1990 acting debut] ‘Herman’ in Haugesund more than 30 years ago, so it feels full circle to receive this honor here,” Anders Danielsen Lie told Variety.


	“I think I dreamed of becoming a great actor when I was a young adult, but I abandoned that dream when I started med school. It was Joachim Trier’s first film that restarted my career,” he said.  

	“I think there are several ‘before’ and ‘after’ moments in my career, with the first being ‘Reprise’. If it weren’t for that film, I would never have worked as an actor.”

	While “Oslo, August 31st” was probably “the biggest turning point” in his career, smash hits “The Worst Person in the World” and “Sentimental Value” – also directed by Trier – introduced him to an even bigger audience. 

	“It’s always hard to say exactly why a film is loved by the audience, but they both tell stories that are relatable to many people. They are very entertaining films, but they also have an almost therapeutic quality to them,” he noted, adding: “I’m a bit surprised I have an international career, because I’ve always been ambivalent about acting – but hopefully that adds an extra layer of complexity to my work!” 
	

	Following “Sentimental Value’s” Oscar win – and nine nominations – Norwegian films definitely have an international momentum at the moment, he noted. 

	“I think there are several reasons for that. One is that we have great funding opportunities for films with limited commercial potential. I think Norwegian cinema as a whole has much more self-confidence now, which has been built up over many years. What we see now is the end result of a long evolution.” 

	Anne Marie Ottersen was surprised by the recognition. 

	“It was totally unexpected, but [it made me] very happy. In theater, most of what we do is gone with the wind once the performance is over. But now I’m written in stone, and that will last almost forever,” she said. 

	Ottersen joined the National Theatre in 1970, and won the Amanda Award for “Wives – Ten Years Later.” Her latest film, “The Pension Heist” directed by Gunnbjörg Gunnarsdóttir, will be released in October.  

	“The best thing I can say about my career is that I have been lucky to do so many different things. There have been difficult periods, of course, but I have the best job in the world, and I’m still working. I’m so happy about that.”

	The Walk of Fame was established in 2015, when actors Kristoffer Joner and Ane Dahl Torp became the first recipients.

	The Norwegian Intl. Film Festival Haugesund runs Aug. 22-28.

title: Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Triumphs Again in Fourth Weekend With $39 Million, ‘Insidious 6’ Launches to $25 Million
description: Long may Peter Parker reign! Sony’s Marvel adventure “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” continues to dominate at the box office, collecting $39 million in
body:
Long may Peter Parker reign! Sony’s Marvel adventure “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” continues to dominate at the box office, collecting $39 million in its fourth weekend of release.

	Despite a smattering of newcomers, Spidey remained at No. 1 ahead of another Sony release, “Insidious: Out of the Further.” Much lower down on box office charts were Lionsgate’s action-thriller “Mutiny,” starring Jason Statham, and Black Bear’s comedy “Spa Weekend,” led by Isla Fisher, Leslie Mann, Anna Faris and Michelle Buteau.
	

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has been unstoppable on the big screen with $855 million in Stateside revenues and $2.22 billion globally to date. It’s the fourth film to surpass $800 million in North America and currently ranks as the third-highest grossing domestic release ever, not far behind 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame” ($858 million) and within reach of 2015’s all-time champ “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” ($936 million).


	With no sign of slowing down, the newest “Spider-Man” is primed to eventually overtake “The Force Awakens” as the biggest movie ever at the domestic box office — and could even be the first to clear $1 billion in North America. Meanwhile, “Brand New Day” is the third-highest grossing movie in history in terms of worldwide grosses, behind just 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.9 billion) and “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.7 billion) and ahead of 2022’s “Avatar: The Way of Water” ($2.3 billion).

	Second place went to “Insidious: Out of the Further” with $25.3 million from 3,303 theaters. The movie also earned $35 million internationally for a global start of $60 million. Domestic ticket sales are behind the franchise’s prior entry, 2023’s “The Red Door,” with $33 million. However, the paranormal sequel cost just $18 million to produce, so it won’t require a huge turnout to reap box office rewards. “Insidious” revolves around a purgatorial place inhabited by the tortured spirits of the dead, and it’s been commercially successful for Sony and Blumhouse, with the five prior installments having generated a combined $800 million worldwide against low budgets. While the 2013 sequel “Insidious: Chapter 2” maintains the record for the biggest debut in the franchise with $40 million, “The Red Door” ranks as the highest-grossing installment to date with $189 million worldwide.
	

	“The drop from [the previous installment’s] opening in July 2023 is substantial but typical of these sequels,” says David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. In general, he notes, “the horror audience is thoroughly engaged.”

	“The Odyssey” landed at No. 3 with a remarkable $19.5 million in its sixth frame, a decline of just 17% from the weekend prior. Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster is the second-biggest movie of the year, as well as the highest-grossing R-rated movie of all time, with $539 million in North America and $1.44 billion worldwide to date.

	“Mutiny” launched in sixth place, on the lower end of expectations with $7.5 million from 2,703 theaters. It’s a weak start against the movie’s $40 million production budget. (Lionsgate acquired North American rights but didn’t finance the film.) Statham plays a former Marine who has to prove his innocence after he’s framed for murdering his billionaire boss. Audiences were kinder to the film than critics, with “Mutiny” scoring a “B+” grade on CinemaScore exit polls and a tepid 50% on Rotten Tomatoes.

	“This is a fair domestic opening,” Gross says. “Overseas is where Statham does particularly well and where the movie should make money.”

	“Spa Weekend” fared even worse, crash-landing at No. 9 with $3.05 million from 2,009 screens. It carries a roughly $20 million price tag and likely won’t earn enough to justify Black Bear’s spend on the R-rated comedy. Directed by Jon Lucas and Scott Moore, the movie follows three burned-out childhood besties who travel to a luxury resort in Palm Springs. “Spa Weekend” also earned a decent “B+” grade on CinemaScore but was saddled with a much harsher 33% on Rotten Tomatoes from film reviewers.

	Two holdover titles, “The End of Oak Street” and “PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie,” rounded out the top five. Both films earned roughly $9 million in their sophomore outings (with each suffering a 60% decline from their respective debuts), so the final order on box office charts won’t be confirmed until Monday.

	“The End of Oak Street,” a prehistoric sci-fi mystery starring Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor, has generated $38 million in North America and $86 million globally. Warner Bros. spent $80 million on the movie, and since theater owners get to keep about half of ticket sales, “Oak Street” needs to gross roughly $200 million to break even in its theatrical run.
	

	“PAW Patrol,” a sequel based on the popular Nickelodeon television series for preschoolers, has earned $35.4 million domestically and $103 million worldwide. It carries a $40 million production budget, which was split between Paramount and Spin Master.

	As popcorn season winds down, cinema operators are rejoicing because it’s already the highest-grossing summer movie season since COVID upended the industry in 2020. Now it’s up to fall releases — including Tom Cruise’s comedy “Digger,” “Practical Magic 2” with Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock, a “Resident Evil” reboot from “Weapons” director Zach Cregger and Colleen Hoover’s “Verity” adaptation led by Hathaway and Dakota Johnson — to sustain the momentum. 

	“There are a lot of cool and original ideas for the fall, which is what everyone wants to see,” exhibitor Chris Randleman of Flix Brewhouse told Variety. He says theater owners aren’t comparing the autumn box office to summer, which is the biggest time of year for moviegoing. “We’re looking at whether we’re better off than we were last [fall]. Even if it’s a low bar, we are definitely going to exceed last year.”

title: ‘Seduction,’ Helmed by Zelito Viana and Marcos Palmeira, to Premiere at the Inffinito Fest in Miami (EXCLUSIVE)
description: GRAMADO, Brazil — “Seduction” (“Sedução”), a feature set in the Amazon Rainforest region and helmed by Zelito Viana and Marcos Palmeira, will have i
body:
GRAMADO, Brazil — “Seduction” (“Sedução”), a feature set in the Amazon Rainforest region and helmed by Zelito Viana and Marcos Palmeira, will have its world premiere on Sept. 11 at the 30th edition of the Inffinito Brazilian Film Festival in Miami. 

	H2O is also releasing in local theaters Miguel Faria Jr.’s doc, “Tom Jobim – Esse Seu Olhar,” in the week of Jan. 25, which marks the celebration of the 100th birthday of the legendary composer of “The Girl From Ipanema,” who died in 1994, said Jorge Peregrino, member of the board of H2O Films, the distributor of both films.
	



	

					Tom Jobim
									Courtesy of Ana Jobim
	



	H2O hosted a panel during the Gramado Film Market at the 2026 edition of the Gramado Film Festival, in Southern Brazil.


	“Seduction” marks the debut as a helmer of Marcos Palmeira, a major actor who starred in dozens of telenovelas, series and films in Brazil over the past 50 years. He toplines and co-directs the pic along with his father Zelito Viana, a vet producer of Cinema Novo classic films and director of several features, such as “Villa-Lobos: A Life of Passion.”

	In the plot, Paulo (Palmeira), a renowned actor, when he learns of his father’s death in the Amazon Rainforest, embarks on a journey to settle his father’s unfinished affairs, faces the rough reality of the region and undergoing a radical transformation.

	“In my opinion it is the best film of Zelito Viana, even better than ‘Villa-Lobos: A Life of Passion,’” Peregrino told Variety. “And it is fair to say, and I believe Zelito will agree with me, that Marcos’ direction work brought a freshness to the film.”
	

	Peregrino stressed the high production value of the pic, lensed in Alter do Chão, in the Amazon region, along the Tapajós River. The pics deals with local issues, such as illegal land grabbing.

	“Seduction” also features two Brazilian film and television stars: Camila Morgado plays Sara Teixeira and Dira Paes portrays Maria Rita Martins in the film.

	The Inffinito Brazilian Film Festival is the largest Brazilian film fest held abroad and a pioneer in the promotion and dissemination of local pics in the international market. It takes place in several cities, such as Miami, NYC, London, Vancouver, Rome, Milan, Madrid, Barcelona, Buenos Aires and Shanghai.

	“Tom Jobim – Esse Seu Olhar” marks the new documentary by Faria Jr, recognized as a top Brazilian director of feature-length docs about music composers. He has helmed the critically acclaimed “Vinicius” (2005), about Vinicius de Moraes, which had a strong box office performance, and “Chico: Artista Brasileiro” (2015), about Chico Buarque, another legend of Brazilian music.

	“Tom Jobim – Esse Seu Olhar” is an Arpoador Audiovisual and Urca Filmes production which is co-produced by Globo Filmes. Peregrino and Leonardo Edde are producing. Diana Vasconcellos co-wrote the doc’s screenplay along with Miguel Faria Jr. and also serves as the film’s editor.

	“Miguel Faria Jr. conducted extensive archival research. He gathered interviews with Tom Jobim from television and other media and edited them in such a way that 70% to 80% of the documentary is narrated by Tom himself,” Peregrino said.

title: ‘Skintown’ Review: A Breezy, Loved-Up, Drugged-Up Guide to Getting Into Trouble in The Troubles
description: Nostalgia, like ecstasy, is a hell of a drug and Kieron J. Walsh’s warm-hearted, hot-headed “Skintown” is buzzing on both. A more polite brother to
body:
Nostalgia, like ecstasy, is a hell of a drug and Kieron J. Walsh’s warm-hearted, hot-headed “Skintown” is buzzing on both. A more polite brother to the “Kneecap” boys and a more cautious cousin to those “Derry Girls” still, the Fermanagh-set friendship comedy sends fizzy, sweetly chemical energy coursing through a rave-romanticizing riff on the coming-of-age formula. The story may not be exactly new, but its bittersweet life lessons are delivered with such retroactive affection and such eagerness by the appealing cast, that if you’re of a mind to complain, well, in the parlance of the movie, would you ever give over, catch yourself on and wise up. 
	

	It is 1994, in Enniskillen, unflatteringly dubbed “Skintown” by its denizens and famous for “a lake, an old castle and an IRA bomb that killed 11 civilians in 1987.” Vinny (Jack Rowan) wants nothing more than to get the hell out. Partly, that’s due to the omnipresent dangers of an intractable conflict that has been ongoing since before he was born. (Vinny is 23, though his characterization here skews younger.) But really his disillusion with Skintown is an independence struggle of a more personal kind — one recognisable to anybody who remembers their jaundiced familiarity with their childhood hometown starting to curdle into contempt as adulthood beckoned. When Vinny strikes up an unlikely friendship with Wilson (Hope Ipoku Jr.) a Black squaddie from Manchester who’s been deployed to serve in the universally despised British military patrols, they bond when he realises that for Wilson, joining the army was his escape from the place he grew up in.
	

	Still, as soon as Vinny gets the money together, he’s resolved to leave, although there are things he’ll miss: his supportive, hardworking paramedic mum (Roisin Gallagher); his peppy unrequited crush Eileen (Jamie Lee O’Donnell); and most of all, his best mate Jonty (Chris Walley), a shell-suited, high-spirited raver just out to have a good time. Vinny and Jonty are as thick as the thieves they eventually, inadvertently become when they’re pressganged into a caper involving a load of ecstasy stolen from the UVF (a loyalist paramilitary group).

	On the bright side, though — and DP Ruairi O’Brien’s pleasant images make most everything bright even when, among sparse crowds and street scenes that feel rigidly dressed to the camera, the limits of the budget show — if they manage to sell the drugs and survive, they stand to make quite a bit of cash. More, anyway, than they could hope to score from their part-time jobs at the neighborhood pizzeria, whose oleaginous owner, splendidly named Tony Pepperoni (Michael Smiley), insists on serving his pizzas with a side of Peking ribs because, he contends, “the Irish aren’t ready for pizza on its own. They need a wee side of ribs to wean them off the Chinese.”

	That kind of authentically eccentric observation feels lifted directly from experience, and the pacy screenplay, adapted by Enniskillen native Ciarán McMenamin from his 2018 novel, abounds in such flourishes. As a ritual, the whole pub greets the TV newsreader (modelled on BBC institution Moira Stuart) like an old friend every time she begins her report with “Good evening.” “Body of Christ,” blasphemes Jonty benignly, handing out pills at a rave like they’re communion wafers. And, it being marching season, everyone is used to maneuvering around the Orangemen who take to parading down the main street at the drop of a bowler hat. “They’d want to get a move on if they’re planning on stopping outside every Catholic pub,” sighs barmaid Chalky (Tara Lynn O’Neill) resignedly. 

	Ah yes, the Catholics. The Protestants. The Republicans. The Unionists. The IRA, the UVF, the UDA, the INLA, the RUC, the Brits and the Battle of the Boyne — Vinny’s rather unnecessary voiceover namechecks them all, with more or less equal disparagement. While he and his mates are from a Catholic/Republican background, “Skintown” is careful not to overtly assign blame to one side and virtue to the other. Instead, most of its rancor is directed without sectarian bias, at the politician class. The brief, incredulous euphoria that follows the fateful announcement of an IRA ceasefire, is immediately dampened by one barfly (Belfast-born icon Lalor Roddy) observing drily, “If there’s any conceivable way to fuck this up, those politicians will find it.”
	

	This careful avoidance of any alienating perspective, and its streak of sentimentality make “Skintown” a more timid proposition than, say, “Kneecap,” even as it ramps up to an inevitable tragedy to undercut the bursts of MDMA-infused idealism elsewhere. But it also serves up a gently pointed reminder that for all the region was internationally synonymous with terrorism, reprisal and violent death, most of its inhabitants were ordinary people just going about the humdrum business of everyday life. And being Northern Irish, they did it with an indomitable sense of humor. So don’t come to “Skintown” for trenchant political commentary; come for the slangy jokes, the ’90s kitsch and the precise evocation of the love/hate relationship so many of us Irish have with the place that, however begrudgingly, we call home.

schema.headline: ‘Skintown’ Review: A Breezy, Loved-Up, Drugged-Up Guide to Getting Into Trouble in The Troubles

title: Venice-Bound ‘Meteorite,’ Debut Feature From Colombia’s Sebastián Múnera, Acquired by MoreThan Films (EXCLUSIVE)
description: MoreThan Films has acquired Colombian filmmaker Sebastián Múnera‘s film “Meteorite,” which will have its world premiere in Venice Critics’ Week (Sep
body:
MoreThan Films has acquired Colombian filmmaker Sebastián Múnera‘s film “Meteorite,” which will have its world premiere in Venice Critics’ Week (Sept. 2-12).

	The film follows Tefa and Nia, who live in a small town near the Magdalena River, where they raise Nia’s young nephew. Nia persuades Tefa to join her in smuggling cellphones into the regional prison. Their journey leads them through an extravagant amusement park built on the grounds of a drug lord’s former estate.
	

	“As they wander among water slides, verdant paths, and concrete dinosaurs, disquieting memories whisper in the summer heat. In a landscape where violence lingers beneath every surface, Tefa is drawn toward an inevitable encounter,” according to the synopsis.


	Queralt Pons Serra, managing partner at MoreThan Films, said, “What excited us about ‘Meteorite’ from the beginning was the strength and singularity of Sebastián’s gaze. You can really feel his artistic background in the way he approaches images, spaces and textures, creating a world that is incredibly cinematic, beautiful and also deeply emotional. There is something very immersive and atmospheric about the film that stayed with us long after watching it.”

	Múnera is a Colombian visual artist and filmmaker. He was a resident at the Cité Internationale des Arts in Paris, invited by the Centre Georges Pompidou. His films have been selected at festivals such as IFFR Rotterdam, DOK Leipzig and FICCI Cartagena. He has received distinctions including the Humberto Solás Cine en Construcción Award and the International Symposium on Auteur Cinema Altiplano Incuba Award.
	

	“Meteorite,” his first fiction feature, was awarded at work-in-progress programs in Málaga and Cartagena.

	The producers are Sebastian Martinez, Mauricio S. Burckhardt (Haus Kino), Valeria Mejia, Sebastián Múnera (Entre Acto), Abel Villa Romero, Deimer Quintero Vertel (Archipiélago Sonoro) and Rodrigo Ramos (Pos[T] La Casa).

schema.headline: Venice-Bound ‘Meteorite,’ Debut Feature From Colombia’s Sebastián Múnera, Acquired by MoreThan Films (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘One Piece’ Season 3 Casts Its Koza, Toto, Pell and Chaka
description:
Netflix has added four to the cast of “One Piece” Season 3, casting the roles of Koza, Toto, Pell and Chaka. 

	Emilio Sakraya (“Rheingold”) will pl
body:
Netflix has added four to the cast of “One Piece” Season 3, casting the roles of Koza, Toto, Pell and Chaka. 

	Emilio Sakraya (“Rheingold”) will play Koza, Omid Abtahi (The Mandalorian”) will play Toto, Jamie Ward (“The Gentlemen”) will play Pell and Nabeel Khan (“Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom”) plays Chaka. 

	Returning for the third season, which is officially titled “One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta,” are Iñaki Godoy as Monkey D. Luffy, Mackenyu as Zoro, Emily Rudd as Nami, Jacob Romero as Usopp, Taz Skylar as Sanji, Charithra Chandran as Miss Wednesday, Mikaela Hoover as Chopper, Joe Manganiello as Mr. 0, Lera Abova as Miss All Sunday and Sendhil Ramamurthy as Nefartari Cobra. 
	

	Season 3 newcomers include Cole Escola as Bon Clay, Xolo Maridueña as Portgas D. Ace, Daisy Head as Miss Doublefinger and Awdo Awdo as Mr. 1. 


	Following the events of the show’s sophomore season, war is brewing for Monkey D. Luffy and the Straw Hat gang in Alabasta, Princess Vivi’s homeland. Per the series logline, “a rebellion threatens to tear the nation apart, fueled in secret by one of the Seven Warlords of the Sea, the ruthless Sir Crocodile, and his underground syndicate Baroque Works, who seek to conquer Alabasta for themselves. In a season defined by unbreakable bonds and impossible choices, the Straw Hats must face a brewing civil war and a powerful warlord to save Vivi’s kingdom before it crumbles into the sand.”

	Joe Tracz and Ian Stokes serve as co-showrunners, writers and executive producers. “One Piece” was created in partnership with Shueisha and produced by Tomorrow Studios and Netflix. 
	

	Executive producing are Eiichiro Oda, Marty Adelstein and Becky Clements through Tomorrow Studios, Tetsu Fujimura, Chris Symes, Christoph Schrewe and Steven Maeda. Production for Season 3 of the pirate adventure has wrapped in Cape Town, South Africa

title: HBO Max Is Free Right Now For 7 Days With This Prime Video Promo
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Despite H
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Despite HBO Max hiking prices again last fall, the streamer is hoping to win over some new customers, with a 7-day free trial through Prime Video, just in time for the buzzy premiere of “Lanterns” and awards season pushes for critically-acclaimed shows like “Hacks” and “The Pitt.”

	While Amazon usually saves its streaming deals for Prime Day, this HBO Max offer is live on the site now and open to all Prime members with no promo code or contract required. In order to access the free trial, you’ll have to sign up for an Amazon Prime account (which also offers a 30-day free trial) and navigate to the Prime Channels hub. From there, find the HBO Max landing page and select the free trial offer.


	If you already have a Prime account, you can just sign in and add an HBO Max account free of charge. Once the week-long trial ends, the ad-supported HBO Max subscription will resume at its regular price of $10.99/month.

	There’s never been a better time to add an HBO Max subscription (formerly “Max”) to your Prime Video streaming arsenal. HBO Max has had an exciting lineup of can’t-miss new releases for 2026, including “DTF St. Louis,” the return of Lisa Kudrow’s “The Comeback” and the “Big Bang Theory” spin-off, “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe.”

	Returning favorites this year also included the third season of “The White Lotus” and the final season of “Euphoria.”

	HBO Max also has hundreds of new films on its roster, including “Marty Supreme,” “The Drama,” “Wuthering Heights,” “We Live in Time,” “Dune: Part Two” and “Joker Folie à Deux,” in addition to beloved shows such as “The Sopranos,” “The Wire” and “Curb Your Enthusiasm.”


	HBO Max doesn’t offer a free trial on its own site, so the Prime Video deal is one of the only ways to get the streaming service for free. Worth noting: Amazon has removed this offer from its Prime streaming hub in the past without warning, so we recommend taking advantage of the free trial while it’s still live.

	You can also get HBO Max for free through DirecTV, which offers a free subscription when you sign-up for the streamer’s MyEntertainment Genre Pack. Plans start at $42.99/month and get you 60+ live TV channels plus HBO Max, Disney+ and Hulu for free. See the DirecTV deal here.

title: ‘One Battle After Another’ and ‘Marty Supreme’ Take Top Honors at Location Managers Guild International Awards
description:
“One Battle After Another” and “Marty Supreme” took top honors at the Location Managers Guild International (LMGI) LMGI Awarda.

	The LGMI Awards we
body:
“One Battle After Another” and “Marty Supreme” took top honors at the Location Managers Guild International (LMGI) LMGI Awarda.

	The LGMI Awards were handed out on Saturday night and honor the use of filming locations across motion pictures, television, commercials, film commissions, and special achievement categories. 

	Paul Thomas Anderson’s “One Battle After Another” won outstanding locations in a contemporary feature film. It was shot across California’s Humboldt County, Sacramento, Stockton, Eureka, Arcata, San Diego and El Paso, Texas. Josh Safdie’s “Marty Supreme” won outstanding locations in a period feature film for its work across New York City, greater New York, the Hudson Valley, New Jersey and Tokyo.
	

	“Pluribus,” “Fallout” and “Black Rabbit” were the television winners. “Pluribus” was filmed in Albuquerque, New Mexico, Montana, Nevada, and Spain, and won outstanding locations in a contemporary television series. “Fallout,” shot in California’s Dumont Dunes, Mojave Desert, Antelope Valley and Santa Clarita,” won outstanding locations in a period television series. Filmed around New York City, including Brooklyn and Manhattan, “Black Rabbit” won outstanding locations in a tv anthology, movie or limited series. 


	Four-time Emmy-winning director and writer Vince Gilliga received the Eva Monley Award for his dedication to storytelling through location over his career and his most recent work on “Pluribus.”

	Mike Fantasia, location manager of films including “Top Gun: Maverick,” “Killers of the Flower Moon” and “Spider-Man: Homecoming” was presented the Lifetime Achievement Award. 
	

	“Celebrating our LMGI winners was a truly remarkable experience,” Nancy Haecker, LMGI Awards Chair, said. “The ceremony was a powerful celebration of achievement, filled with inspiring moments and well-deserved recognition, beautifully capped by the genius of Vince Gilligan. Each of this year’s winners is incredibly deserving, and it was a distinct privilege to honor their talent, dedication, and outstanding contributions to our industry.”

	Winners list below.

	OUTSTANDING LOCATIONS IN A CONTEMPORARY FEATURE FILM

	“One Battle After Another” (Warner Bros. Pictures)

	Michael Glaser / LMGI, Michael Wesley / LMGI, Rich Heichel / LMGI

	OUTSTANDING LOCATIONS IN A PERIOD FEATURE FILM

	“Marty Supreme” (A24)

	Matthew Kania, Ross Brodar / LMGI

	OUTSTANDING LOCATIONS IN A CONTEMPORARY TELEVISION SERIES

	“Pluribus” (Apple TV+)

	Christian Diaz de Bedoya / LMGI, John O’Connor, Priscila Calero, Jorge Noguerales,

	Yanira De Armas, Will Brewster

	OUTSTANDING LOCATIONS IN A PERIOD TELEVISION SERIES

	“Fallout” – Season 2 (Amazon Prime Video)

	Mandi Dillin / LMGI, David Park / LMGI

	OUTSTANDING LOCATIONS IN A TV ANTHOLOGY, MOVIE OR LIMITED SERIES

	“Black Rabbit” (Netflix)

	Paul Eskenazi, Joel McGlumphy

	OUTSTANDING FILM COMMISSION/ OFFICE

	Humboldt-Del Norte Film Commission: “One Battle After Another” (Warner Bros. Pictures)

	Cassandra Hesseltine

	OUTSTANDING LOCATIONS IN A COMMERCIAL

	TOYOTA TRUCKS: “They Don’t Read Reviews”

	Alexandra Gibson / LMGI, Christina Conway / LMGI

title: Upendra Joins Cast as Teja Sajja, Shanaya Kapoor, Suparn S. Varma’s Sequel Titled ‘Zombie Reddy Nxt Lvl’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Kannada cinema superstar Upendra has joined the cast of “Zombie Reddy Nxt Lvl,” the sequel to the hit “Zombie Reddy,” in a powerhouse role, India’s
body:
Kannada cinema superstar Upendra has joined the cast of “Zombie Reddy Nxt Lvl,” the sequel to the hit “Zombie Reddy,” in a powerhouse role, India’s People Media Factory has confirmed. 

	The announcement, made on star Teja Sajja‘s birthday, also confirms the film’s cast and creative team.

	The adventure zombie action-comedy marks the South Indian cinema debut of “Tu Yaa Main” star Shanaya Kapoor. Teja Sajja returns as the franchise’s zombie-slaying lead.
	

	Directed by Prasanth Varma, “Zombie Reddy” was released in 2021, and followed a game developer who must save his village after a scientist’s vaccine experiment unleashes a zombie outbreak. 


	Suparn S. Varma, known for Prime Video’s “The Family Man” Season 2, Netflix’s “Rana Naidu” and film “Haq,” directs the sequel from a story created by Prasanth Varma. Gowra Hari, whose scores powered “HanuMan” and “Mirai,” composes the music.

	Hussain Dalal, Prasanth Varma and Suparn S. Varma wrote the screenplay. T.G. Vishwa Prasad and Krithi Prasad produce for People Media Factory. The film will release in seven languages – Hindi, Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, Malayalam, Nepali and Japanese.

	“The biggest takeaway from my career is that cinema survives on audacity, not formulas,” Teja Sajja said. “When ‘Zombie Reddy’ was made, it was a calculated risk born out of a desire to break the monotony of conventional storytelling. I can’t thank the audience enough for embracing me as a zombie slayer and their unbridled curiosity and faith in what I do next. It’s the love that I’ve received over the years that pushes me to make brave choices. So here’s a promise to take the mayhem to a whole new scale in ‘Zombie Reddy Nxt Lvl.’ As I turn a year older, the zombies turn deadlier. With the audience validating everyone associated with the film, I’m all set to fight the dead onscreen like never before. It makes me very proud to be part of a team that wants to give viewers a grand, immersive spectacle that feeds their appetite for the extraordinary.”
	

	Suparn S. Varma said the goal was to surprise both himself and the audience with something unlike anything seen before. “Zombies have always been a fascinating expression of our worst catastrophes, and with this film, we wanted to take that idea to the next level,” he said. “We’ve taken the foundational brilliance that Prasanth Varma created and blown it wide open, building a never-seen-before zombieverse. It’s been an absolute treat to explore a genre with such enormous creative possibilities and collaborate with stalwarts who bring their own seasoned finesse to the film. Here’s wishing one of them – the audience’s superstar and favourite zombie slayer, Teja Sajja, a very happy birthday!”

	T.G. Vishwa Prasad said People Media Factory has always aimed to push the boundaries of commercial cinema. “‘Zombie Reddy Nxt Lvl’ is an epic adventure designed for a global audience, which is why we are releasing it from India to Japan,” he said. “Everything is next level right from the actors starring in it to the director, technicians, and music. The scale is massive, the stakes are dead or alive, and we cannot wait to bring this zombieverse to audiences in 2027.”

schema.headline: Upendra Joins Cast as Teja Sajja, Shanaya Kapoor, Suparn S. Varma’s Sequel Titled ‘Zombie Reddy Nxt Lvl’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Dr. Dre Says the Only People Who See AI as a Threat Are Those ‘Who Have Trouble Creating’
description: Dr. Dre, the legendary hip-hop producer and performer, sees AI as another tool in the music-tech toolbox akin to synthesizers — and asserted that on
body:
Dr. Dre, the legendary hip-hop producer and performer, sees AI as another tool in the music-tech toolbox akin to synthesizers — and asserted that only people “who have trouble creating” are afraid of AI.

	Dre, founder of the Aftermath record label and co-founder and CEO of Apple’s Beats, said that he doesn’t see AI “as a threat,” in an interview alongside his longtime business partner Jimmy Iovine, which was published Sunday by the New York Times. “I think the only people that see it as a threat are the people who have trouble creating.”
	

	“I had a discussion with a few people a few days ago,” Dre said. “They were against AI and I’m like, ‘OK, you sound like the person that would have been against the drum machine when it came out.’ Or synthesizers, right? It’s a new tool for creativity. Some people are afraid of learning new things.”


	Dre said he’s using AI tech in music “as a tool to see what it would do with what I just did.” Iovine added, “So is Timbaland — another brilliant producer. By the way, there’s a lot of closet AI producers out there.”

	Asked what he most recently asked an AI chatbot, Dre said his query was, “How do you put on muscle and lose fat at the same time? That’s it.”

	Dre, 61, was named to Forbes’ 2026 Billionaires list, joining the publication’s rankings for the first time, with an estimated net worth of $1 billion. In 2014, he and Iovine sold Beats by Dre to Apple in a deal worth more than $3 billion. Dre in 2023 sold a collection of music income streams and other assets to Shamrock Holdings and Universal Music Group for more than $200 million.
	

	In the music industry, AI remains controversial and the subject of ongoing legal disputes. For example, last week indie music publisher Round Hill Music sued Suno and Anthropic, accusing the two AI companies of copyright infringement by illegally scraping hundreds of its songs to train their models without permission. Suno has been sued by all three of the major labels — Warner Music Group, Universal Music Group and Sony Music — though it settled with WMG last year. In addition, Suno recently struck a licensing agreement with BMG (which sued Anthropic this year for allegedly using its recordings to train AI models in what it called a scheme of “widespread and systematic infringement”).

	Meanwhile, Apple Music said it will begin labeling songs derived from AI platforms later this year, following Spotify’s decision to label the profiles of artists that appear to be AI-generated as “AI Personas.” Last month, a coalition including the RIAA, IFPI, the Grammys and SAG-AFTRA united to advocate for a new industry labeling program for AI-produced songs similar to labels flagging explicit content.

	Corbin Bolies contributed to this article.

schema.headline: Dr. Dre Says the Only People Who See AI as a Threat Are Those ‘Who Have Trouble Creating’

            Jay Leno wants courts in New Hampshire to recognize his wife's conservatorship in California so he can sell one of their New England properties ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Jay says he's planning to sell some real estate he and his wife, Mavis, own in the Granite State ... hence the reason for the filing.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            TMZ obtained court docs filed earlier this month, where the comedian tells the court he wants to sell "certain real estate located in New Hampshire" that they hold as community property.
      

                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            The property in question appears to be a 2-bed, 2-bath ranch built in 1995 ... that he's listed for just under $400K. Jay put it up for sale back in June.
      
    
            He's been Mavis' caretaker throughout her battle with dementia.
      
    
            The court has yet to rule.

body:
Meghan Markle
                          Say 'Cheerio' To My Acting Comeback ...
                          Casting in 'The Gentleman' Reportedly Withdrawn
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 22, 2026
                            5:16 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Meghan Markle's return to acting might not be happening after all ... because a new report indicates "The Gentleman" ran scared from the star due to fan outrage.
      
    
            Here's the deal ... reports began circulating this week that Meghan was being considered for a part in Guy Ritchie's hit series -- though the talks were in very early stages.
      
    
            However, on Saturday, Tina Brown -- formerly the editor-in-chief at Vanity Fair and The New Yorker -- says the dream is already dead ... and it was a much more serious offer than initial reports indicated.
      

            She wrote on her Substack, "I learned this morning that the casting of Meghan Markle in season 3 of Guy Ritchie’s Netflix series 'The Gentlemen' has been withdrawn. The backlash in the UK was so intense, it became untenable to go forward. This does not bode well for Meghan’s acting comeback in the UK.”
      
    
            Worth noting ... even if the casting hadn't been withdrawn, Meghan wouldn't have appeared in the upcoming season of the show because it comes out next month. Her character was supposed to appear in season 3 ... if Netflix decides to renew the series.
      
    
            As you know ... Meghan and Harry are temporarily moving to the UK with their two children -- Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet -- in a shocking relocation.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Harry's father -- King Charles -- was told of the development earlier this week ... and reports say he's excited to spend time with his son's family.
      
    
            The reason for the move is still a mystery ... though, if it was connected to this reported offer, it makes you wonder if they'll still go through with the move.
